Crs) Q2FY27 Q2FY26 Y-o-Y Q1FY27 Q-o-Q H1 FY27 H1 FY26 Y-o-Y Revenue 1,556 1,156 35% 1,364 14% 2,919 2,183 34% EBITDA (incl. other income) 228 170 34% 205 11% 434 306 42% Margin (%) 14.7% 14.7% 15.1% 14.9% 14.0% PBT 154 104 48% 132 17% 286 179 60% Margin (%) 9.9% 9.0% 9.7% 9.8% 8.2% PAT before Minority Interest 117 78 50% 99 18% 215 132 64% Margin (%) 7.5% 6.7% 7.2% 7.4% 6.0% EPS 15.48 9.81 58% 12.71 22% 28.19 15.89 77% Gurugram, October 24, 2026 – Lumax Auto Technologies Limited (NSE: LUMAXTECH, BSE: 532796), a leading automotive component manufacturer, today announced its unaudited financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30th 2026, and continued to strengthen its growth trajectory through technology-led expansion, portfolio diversification and operational excellence. Consolidated Financial Highlights for Q2 & H1 FY27: • Strong Revenue Growth: Consolidated revenue from operations grew by 35% YoY in Q2FY27 crossing the ₹1,500 mark for the first time to reach ₹1,556 crore, from ₹1,156 crore in Q2FY26, and by 34% YoY in H1FY27 to ₹2,919 crore, reflecting consistent scale-up across core product categories, increasing wallet share with OEMs and premiumization-led value enhancement. • Enhanced Profitability: § EBITDA stood at ₹ 228 crores for Q2FY27 compared to ₹ 170 crores in Q2FY26, a growth of 34% Y-o-Y. EBITDA margins stood at 14.7%, broadly stable YoY, marginally declining QoQ amid rising input costs and associated recoveries from OEMs. For H1FY27, EBITDA grew 42% Y-o-Y to ₹ 434 crores, with margins at 14.9%, an increase of ~90 bps YoY on the back of operational efficiencies, cost optimization and a favorable product mix. § PAT (before minority interest) for Q2FY27 stood at ₹ 117 crores, growth of 50% Y-o-Y, with margins at 7.5% (+80 bps Y-o-Y). For H1FY27, PAT (before minority interest) grew 64% Y-o-Y to ₹ 215 crores, driven by technologically led operational excellence and improving asset turns and utilizations. The Bank reported Profit After Tax of ₹1,045 crore in Q2 FY27, up 196.5% year-on-year. For H1 FY27, Profit After Tax stood at ₹2,120 crore, with Return on Assets at 0.99%. Management Commentary 1. Loan growth: Loans and advances, including credit substitutes and FCNR(B)-backed loans, grew 30.1% YoY to ₹3,46,913 crore. Excluding loans secured by FCNR(B) deposits, loan growth was 22.2%, gross of IBPC. 4. Operating leverage: Opex growth has remained lower than income growth by about 500 bps YoY for consecutive quarters. 5. Improving cost-to-income ratio: Incremental cost-to-income ratio was 55% in H1 FY27. The core cost-to-income ratio (excluding trading gains) improved to 70.16% in Q2 FY27 from 70.73% in Q1 FY27. 6. Strong growth in core operating profit: Core operating profit, excluding trading gains, grew 38.5% YoY to ₹2,527 crore in Q2 FY27. 7. Stable asset quality: GNPA stood at 1.32% and Net NPA at 0.40%. FCNR(B) mobilisation: During Q2 FY27, the Bank mobilised ₹34,390 crore (approximately US$3.6 billion) of FCNR(B) deposits despite having no branch, subsidiary or representative office outside India. Cement Limited (“the Company”), at its meeting held today i.e. October 24, 2026, has, inter alia, considered and approved the following: 1) Unaudited Financial Results: Approved the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 (“Financial Results”); 2) Amendment to Insider Trading Code: The Board of Directors has approved amendments to the Code of Conduct for Regulating, Monitoring and Reporting of Trading by Designated Persons and the Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information of the Company, effective immediately. The amended Code is enclosed herewith as Annexure - A. 3) Appointment of Statutory Auditors: Based on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, the Board has recommended the appointment of Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP (ICAI Firm Registration No. 012754N/N500016) as the Statutory Auditors of the Company, to hold office for a term of 5 (five) consecutive years from the conclusion of the 33rd Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) of the Company to be held in the year 2027 till the conclusion of the 38th AGM to be held in the year 2032, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company and such other statutory requirements as may be applicable, including confirmation of eligibility and independence under Sections 139 and 141 of the Company’s Act, 2013 (the Act). Kotak Mahindra Bank standalone results During the quarter, the Bank mobilised FCNR(B) deposits aggregating to ~₹ 55,344 crore and provided loans aggregating to ~₹ 16,110 crore through it’s international branches. The Bank’s PAT for Q2FY27 increased to ₹ 4,212 crore, up 29% YoY from ₹ 3,253 crore in Q2FY26 (up 2% QoQ from ₹ 4,123 crore in Q1FY27). Net Interest Income (NII) for Q2FY27 increased to ₹ 8,459 crore, up 16% YoY from ₹ 7,311 crore in Q2FY26 (up 7% QoQ from ₹ 7,928 crore in Q1FY27). Net Interest Margin (NIM) for Q2FY27 stood at 4.31% versus 4.54% in Q2FY26 and 4.53% in Q1FY27. The moderation in NIM was largely on account of FCNR(B) mobilisation during the quarter. Cost of funds was 4.52% for Q2FY27 (4.70% for Q2FY26 and 4.46% for Q1FY27). Fees and services for Q2FY27 increased to ₹ 2,926 crore, up 21% YoY from ₹ 2,415 crore in Q2FY26 (up 17% QoQ from ₹ 2,500 crore in Q1FY27). Operating expenses for Q2FY27 increased to ₹ 5,271 crore, up 14% YoY from ₹ 4,632 crore in Q2FY26 (up 3% QoQ from ₹ 5,135 crore in Q1FY27). Cost to assets improved to 2.40% for Q2FY27 (2.67% for Q2FY26 and 2.66% for Q1FY27). Thank you, Yours faithfully, For Tembo Global Industries Limited ___________________ Sanjay Jashbhai Patel Managing Director DIN: 01958033 Tembo Global Industries Performs Bhoomi Poojan for Its Defence Manufacturing Facility in Amravati, Maharashtra Marks a key milestone in the Group’s expansion into small arms and ammunition manufacturing Tembo Global Industries Limited, listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE: TEMBO) and BSE Limited, today marked a significant milestone in its expansion into defence manufacturing with the Bhoomi Poojan ceremony for its proposed defence manufacturing facility in Amravati, Maharashtra. The ceremony represents a significant step forward in the Group’s efforts to establish a dedicated manufacturing presence in the defence and security sector, complementing its established engineering, industrial products and infrastructure businesses. The proposed facility is being developed through the Company’s subsidiary, Tembo Classic Engineering Private Limited (TCEPL), as part of its long-term strategy to build capabilities in small arms and ammunition manufacturing. The Amravati project builds on the Group’s earlier initiatives to enter the defence manufacturing sector, including its strategic engagement with the Government of Maharashtra and the development of its proposed manufacturing facility in the state. The project is aligned with India’s broader objectives of strengthening domestic defence production, encouraging indigenous manufacturing and reducing dependence on imports in strategically important sectors. TCEPL has received a licence from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, for the manufacture of ammunition of various calibres and has also obtained a small-arms manufacturing licence. These regulatory milestones provide an important foundation for the development of the Group’s defence manufacturing capabilities, subject to applicable statutory requirements and project implementation. The Company intends to progressively develop the infrastructure, manufacturing capabilities and operational readiness required to support its planned entry into the arms and ammunition market. The project is expected to strengthen Tembo’s strategic positioning in a sector where domestic manufacturing capabilities, technology development and supply-chain resilience remain important national priorities. Through this initiative, Tembo Global Industries aims to build a platform for participation in relevant domestic and international defence markets, subject to applicable regulations, customer requirements and export authorisations. The project also reflects the Group’s broader diversification strategy, which seeks to create additional long-term growth opportunities alongside its existing businesses. The project is proposed to be implemented in phases up to FY 2030-31. The relevant details as required under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 as updated on 30th January 2026 is attached as Annexure. Approved capital expenditure and capacity expansion Sno Particulars Details a) Existing capacity The current consolidated installed capacity for sheet metal (lamination) is 1,08,000 MT per annum and for machining hours is 8,13,600 with an approved expansion currently underway to enhance machining capacity to 10,80,000 machining hours by Q1 2029-30. b) Existing capacity utilization The current capacity utilisation stands at ~ 78% for sheet metal and ~ 85% for machining. c) Proposed capacity addition Particulars Existing On-going Post (Per annum) Capacity as Capacity Proposed on addition to be Capacity 30-Sep-2026 completed by Q1 2029-30 Sheet Metal (MT) 1,08,000 NA 1,60,000 Machine Hours 8,13,600 10,80,000 13,14,000 d) Period within which the proposed The project is proposed to be implemented in phases up to FY 2030-31. capacity is to be added e) Investment required Estimated project cost is ₹ 450 crores f) Mode of financing Internal accruals and Debt g) Rationale The Company is witnessing sustained growth in demand across key sectors, including mining and off-highway vehicles, power generation (including thermal, hydro, pumped storage and wind energy), data centres, railways and metro infrastructure. Ltd., a leading building materials Company in India, announced its financial results for the year ended September 30, 2026. Nuvoco completed ten years in the cement business this year. What began in 2014 with a single manufacturing operation at Nimbol with 2.3 MMTPA cement capacity has grown into a diversified building-materials company spanning Cement, Ready-Mix Concrete, and Modern Building Materials. We have sustained our growth journey across market cycles and are now well positioned to reach 35 MMTPA of cement capacity by FY28, nearly 15x growth over the past decade. The Company achieved cement sales volume of 4.7 MMT in Q2 FY27, registering a 9% YoY growth. Consolidated Revenue grew 13.5% YoY to Rs. 2790 Cr. in Q2 FY27. The Company also reported a growth of 11% YoY in EBITDA to Rs 411 Cr. in Q2 FY27. On the sustainability and cost-efficiency front, the Company partnered with CleanMax for a 46.4 MW wind–solar hybrid renewable energy project in Rajasthan. Once operational, the project is expected to generate approximately 100 million units of renewable electricity annually and deliver long-term cost certainty by reducing dependence on conventional power sources, thereby strengthening the Company’s energy mix and improving long-term cost efficiency across Rajasthan operations. Commenting on the performance of the Company, Mr. Jayakumar Krishnaswamy, Managing Director, Nuvoco Vistas Corp. Ltd., stated, “Q2 FY27 was a testament to resilient execution in a challenging operating environment. Mumbai, October 22, 2026: Rallis India Limited (A TATA Enterprise), a leading player in the Indian agri- inputs industry, announced its financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. Key Highlights: Q2 & H1 FY27 Announcing the results, Dr. Gyanendra Shukla, Managing Director & CEO, Rallis India Limited, said: Rallis navigated a disruptive business environment during Q2 FY27 by focussing on portfolio and operational efficiencies. During the quarter, the Company recorded revenue of ₹858 crore, compared to ₹861 crore in Q2 FY26. PAT stood at ₹85 crore, compared to ₹102 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, while EBITDA stood at ₹126 crore, against ₹154 crore in Q2 FY26. The Company’s EBITDA margin stood at 14.7%, while PAT margin was 9.9%. For the half year ended September 2026, Rallis reported revenue of ₹1,880 crore, compared to ₹1,818 crore in H1 FY26. EBITDA stood at ₹311 crore, against ₹304 crore in the previous year, while PAT stood at ₹210 crore, compared to ₹197 crore in H1 FY26. The Company’s EBITDA margin was 16.5%, while PAT margin stood at 11.2%. Business Performance: Q2 FY27 The Crop Care business recorded topline growth of 4%, primarily driven by 17% growth in the B2B segment with a strong recovery in CSM portfolio. Domestic Formulations (B2C) remained flat year-on- year, supported by 16% growth in herbicides, while insecticides registered flat growth. The Soil & Plant Health (SPH) business recorded 22% growth, primarily driven by price growth. During the quarter, in the Crop Care category, Rallis launched four new products—Silentra (Insecticide), Marcellus (Fungicide), Blitox Super (Fungicide) and Trynage (Herbicide). The new products cater to critical crop-pest segments like Rice BPH and sheath blight segments, sugarcane herbicide and disease control in key horticulture crop. The Seeds business recorded a decline, primarily due to higher returns from the Kharif season. Management Comment Weather-related disruptions and delayed sowing continued to impact market demand during the quarter/season. We remain focused on improving market execution, driving cost efficiencies and strengthening customer engagement to navigate these challenges and enhance business performance. Thanking you Yours f aithfully For Jammu and Kashmir Bank Limited (Mohammad Shafi Mir) Company Secretary PRESS RELEASE J&K Bank’s Q2 net profit rises 28.8% QoQ and 10.6% YoY to Rs 546 Cr Business grows 19.4% to Rs 3.10 lakh Cr, with decadal best asset quality metrics Srinagar, Oct 22: Supported by growth in earnings and further improvement in asset quality, J&K Bank today reported 28.8% rise quarter-on-quarter and 10.6% rise year- on-year in its net profit to Rs 546.36 Cr for the quarter (Q2) ended September 30, 2026, when compared with Rs 424.18 Cr and Rs 494.11 Cr recorded during Q1 FY 2026-27 and Q2 FY 2025-26 respectively. The Bank announced the financial results after its Board of Directors reviewed and approved the quarterly and half-yearly figures at a meeting held at the Bank’s corporate headquarters on 22nd October 2026. Operating Performance The Bank’s Net Interest Income (NII) rose 5% YoY during the quarter to Rs 1502 Cr. During the quarter, other income doubled to Rs 314.90 Cr YoY from Rs 153.76 Cr recorded in the corresponding quarter last year while also growing 47% sequentially. With controlled operating expenditure, witnessing just 1.5% YoY growth for the half- year, the operating Profit for the half-year has also grown by over 15% YoY, being recorded at Rs.1,492 crores. The Cost-to-Income Ratio for the quarter has consequently witnessed substantial improvement, being recorded at 56.57% compared 60.79% for the corresponding quarter last year. The Bank’s Return on Assets during the quarter jumped 20 bps sequentially and has been recorded at 1.07%. Commenting on the financial performance, MD & CEO Amitava Chatterjee said, “The growth in net interest income, doubling of other income and over 26% YoY increase in operating profit for this quarter mark an encouraging strengthening of our earnings performance. The recovery in Return on Assets to above 1% further underlines the improvement over the June quarter.” “In Q1, we had emphasized building the business base and positioning the Bank for stronger earnings over time. This quarter’s operating performance represents progress in that direction. Our focus for the second half is on sustaining core income growth, strengthening recurring revenue streams and enhancing recoveries, while addressing funding costs through deeper deposit relationships. corporate_announcements.pdf_extracted_text: Date: October 22, 2026 To, To, Listing Department Listing Department National Stock Exchange of India Limited BSE Limited Exchange Plaza, C-1, Block-G, Phiroze Jeejeebhoy Towers, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra (E), Dalal Street, Fort, Mumbai-400051 Mumbai-400001 Sub: Board Comments on the fine levied by the Exchanges (NSE and BSE) Ref: Kotyark Industries Limited | ISIN: INE0J0B01017 | NSE Symbol: KOTYARK | BSE Scrip Code: 544726 ==================================================================================== Dear Sir / Madam, With reference to the communications received from National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSE”) and BSE Limited (“BSE”) by mail on September 11, 2026, regarding the imposition of fines for delayed submission of the unaudited financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, under Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), we wish to submit the comments of the Board of Directors on the matter. The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on October 21, 2026, considered and took note of the aforesaid non-compliance and the fines imposed by the Stock Exchanges. The Board noted that the delay in submission of the financial results arose due to the unwillingness of the erstwhile Statutory Auditors, M/s. Manubhai & Shah LLP, to seek re-appointment for a second term, owing to their existing professional commitments and logistical constraints. Consequently, the appointment of M/s. Talati & Talati LLP, as the Statutory Auditors for the financial year 2026-27 was proposed, subject to the approval of the Members at the Company's 10th Annual General Meeting held on August 22, 2026. The transition between the erstwhile and newly appointed Statutory Auditors resulted in a delay in completing the limited review of the financial results and, consequently, in convening the Board Meeting for consideration and approval of the financial results within the prescribed timeline. The Board noted that the Company subsequently submitted its unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, along with the Limited Review Reports, to the Stock Exchanges on September 07, 2026. The Company has also paid the fines imposed by NSE and BSE on September 12, 2026. The Board expressed its concern regarding the delay in compliance with the prescribed regulatory timeline and emphasized the importance of timely compliance with the applicable provisions of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The Board has advised the management to strengthen advance planning and coordination with the Statutory Auditors, establish appropriate internal monitoring mechanisms, and take necessary preventive measures to ensure timely preparation, approval and submission of financial results in future. The Company assures the Stock Exchanges that due care shall be taken to ensure timely compliance with the applicable regulatory requirements going forward. Kindly take the above comments of the Board of Directors on record. Thanking You. Yours Faithfully, For, Kotyark Industries Limited ____________ Bhavesh Nagar Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Membership No. A62546

The facility has an approved manufacturing capacity of ~ 4.4 million BL per annum. The greenfield facility marks a key milestone in expanding ABD’s domestic production footprint and vertically integrating its core supply chain. The facility will enable ABD to manufacture malt spirit in-house, giving the Company greater control over the important input used in its whisky portfolio. This will help ensure consistent quality and provide a steady, dependable supply of malt spirit as production scales up. Along with meeting ABD’s internal needs, the distillery will drive new product development and maturation. Crucially, it allows ABD to begin laying down malt spirit to craft its own homegrown single malt whisky in the coming years and support its growing Prestige & Above portfolio. Commenting on the commencement, Amar Sinha, Managing Director, ABD, said, “The start of operations at the malt distillery is an important step at ABD, this underscores ABD’s disciplined approach to backward integration and process excellence. Moving critical production inputs in-house enhances operating margins, insulates core brands from market fluctuations, and establishes a robust foundation for next-generation spirits development.” Rangapur has evolved into the operational anchor of ABD’s growth story. With grain distillation, PET bottle production, bottling operations, and now with malt distillation, ABD has created an end-to-end, integrated manufacturing hub.
